thread:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: Elevated 5xx rate detected on dedicated-cluster eu-west-1 pool-42. Affected tenant: Pinpoint (customer-id: tn-8374). Error rate 5xx > 8% for 5m. Paging on-call.
ops-rotation: oncall-ack. I'm on it, pinging SRE.
devon (SRE): I see the spike in Grafana. Dashboards: `dedicated/pool-42/errors` and `per-tenant/tn-8374/latency`. 5xx are mostly 502/504 gateway errors.
priya (Eng): joining. Any recent deploys to pool-42 or Pinpoint's model variants?
jamal (Platform): No deploys in the last 30m. Autoscaler logs show sustained pending queue growth and GPU util ~98% on 4 nodes.
maria (Support): Pinpoint support incoming: customer reports timeouts for ~30m, a few production jobs failing. They said "sudden errors". Passing them the incident link.
devon (SRE): Logs show a lot of KV eviction warnings and repeated connection resets to worker-03: `rpc: connection reset by peer`.
alex (Infra): worker-03 is on host gw-eu-42-03, OOM events? Kube shows kubelet evicting pods due to ephemeral-storage pressure.
priya (Eng): Could be noisy tenant causing cache thrash or driving sequence length skew. Any large seq-length requests from tn-8374?
devon (SRE): Sampled traces show many long-context requests (seq > 12k tokens) from Pinpoint's newer batch pipeline. Prefetching appears disabled.
jamal (Platform): Pool has 3 other tenants. Batching config is default continuousBatching=on. If one tenant sends very long contexts it's likely pushing KV usage and spilling to disk.
ops-rotation: Immediate mitigation options: 1) Reroute tn-8374 to a different pool/region; 2) Throttle tenant at gateway; 3) Add emergency burst-capacity (spin new nodes); 4) Nail down culprit requests and ask customer to pause. What do we want now?
priya (Eng): Throttling at gateway is fastest. We can apply a per-tenant QPS cap and reject very long requests (>8k tokens) with 413. That buys time.
maria (Support): I'll ask Pinpoint to pause their bulk-run pipelines while we stabilize. Sending them suggested cURL to pause: `POST /v1/customer/pause?job=bulk`.
devon (SRE): I'll open a temporary route in the routing layer to send tn-8374 to pool-99 (cold spare) while we investigate. pool-99 has 4x V100s but higher latency; acceptable as fallback.
jamal (Platform): I'll prepare pool-99, but note model variants on pool-99 may be quantized; quality may differ. Confirm fallback policy for Pinpoint?
priya (Eng): Pinpoint SLA allows fallback with notice. Maria, confirm customer OK with degraded latency/quality.
maria (Support): Pinpoint agreed to fallback for the next 60m. They paused bulk jobs.
ops-rotation: Devon, can you push the routing change? Include fallback header and rate limit to 20r/s.
devon (SRE): Pushing route now. Command:
```
redwood route update --tenant tn-8374 --route pool-99 --max-qps 20 --fallback=enable
```
devon (SRE): Route update accepted. Verifying traffic shift...
devon (SRE): Metrics: 85% traffic shifted to pool-99 in 90s. 5xx rate for tn-8374 dropped from 8% -> 1.4% on pool-99, overall pool-42 5xx dropped to 3.2%.
alex (Infra): On worker-03 we still see evictions. I'll cordon and drain it to prevent further noisy behavior: `kubectl cordon gw-eu-42-03` then `kubectl drain`.
alex (Infra): Node drained, pods rescheduled. Some pods are pending due to GPU pressure.
jamal (Platform): Spinning two additional nodes in pool-42 as emergency burst. ETA ~3m.
priya (Eng): While nodes spin up, let's keep the per-tenant throttle to avoid hitting disk-backed KV cache. Also enable prefix caching for tn-8374's frequent prompts if possible.
devon (SRE): Enabled per-tenant throttle config (20r/s) and token-length cap at 8k. Also set `kv_cache.min_in_memory_fraction=0.7` for pool-42 to prefer in-RAM KV.
priya (Eng): Good. Enabling prefix caching requires model-awareness; I'll flip a config flag on pool-42 for tn-8374 only.
jamal (Platform): New nodes are up and joining pool-42. GPU util now 78% across pool. Pending queue reduced by 60%.
devon (SRE): 5xx rate now steady at 0.8% for pool-42. No new 502/504s in last 4m.
maria (Support): Customer updated: errors dropped and their team re-enabled jobs slowly. They asked what happened.
priya (Eng): Root cause summary: Pinpoint started a high-concurrency long-context batch workload that saturated KV memory, causing eviction and disk spill leading to worker instability and gateway timeouts. Contributing factors: no per-tenant QPS cap, unbounded sequence lengths, pool-42 running near capacity.
ops-rotation: Action items (owner, ETA):
- short: keep throttle (devon) - until tomorrow 0900 UTC
- infra: investigate node evictions and ephemeral-storage config (alex) - 48h
- platform: add automatic per-tenant seq-length guardrail + alert (jamal) - 7d
- eng: document prefix-caching setup and enable per-tenant by default (priya) - 10d
- support: follow up with Pinpoint about optimized batching (maria) - 24h

priya (Eng): Suggest follow-up improvement: when per-tenant KV mem crosses 60%, trigger autoscale (scale out) and temporary per-tenant throttles automatically.
devon (SRE): I'll add a dashboard and an alert rule: `tenant_kv_mem_pct > 60 -> notify oncall & trigger throttle-playbook`.
jamal (Platform): We'll also consider a hard limit on request token length at the gateway (configurable per-customer). This would have prevented the spike.
maria (Support): Pinpoint appreciated the fast turnaround. They've asked for a post-incident summary. I'll prepare a customer-facing note.
ops-rotation: Closing incident thread here. If anything new pops, reopen. Good work team. :tada:
oncall-bot: INCIDENT: resolved (4810001234) — duration 45m. Severity: P2. Postmortem requested.
